Principle driven.tell: He answers to principle before profit.

good.text: Appeal to his convictions and the principles he has already stated.

bad.text: Appeal to his business interests and what independence would pay him.

Pragmatic.tell: He weighs what works, not what is right.

good.text: Lay out the practical costs and benefits for his own colony.

bad.text: Appeal to lofty ideals and to his sense of moral duty.

Conservative.tell: He fears upheaval more than he fears the Crown.

good.text: Assure him that order, property and established institutions will be protected.

bad.text: Urge him to act decisively and set aside his caution.

Social influencer.tell: He moves crowds with a good story.

good.text: Make the appeal public and stirring — speak to his standing and influence.

bad.text: Appeal to his private doubts and to the hard losses of his trade.

Constituency first.tell: He answers to his constituents, not to principle.

good.text: Speak to the needs of the people and communities he represents.

bad.text: Appeal to his personal ambition and his own standing.

Moderate.tell: He will not be pushed, but he can be brought along.

good.text: Offer a moderate, reconcilable step and a way to go along with it.

bad.text: Push him toward an extreme position and demand a firm answer.
